excellent: They came to lessons ready to try, and they explained their thinking clearly to the people beside them. That habit of showing how they worked is a real strength.
Reading, number work and group tasks all showed care this term. They also helped a classmate settle without being asked.
They stayed with a hard task until it made sense, then used that idea in the next piece of work. It was a pleasure to watch the effort turn into confidence.
Their questions pushed the class further, and the work they handed in was complete and carefully set out. They can be proud of how they used their time.
They listened, had a go, and then checked what they had done. The same care showed up in the way they treated other learners.
They took a lead kindly and still left room for everyone else to speak. The work they finished matched that thoughtfulness.
very_good: They handled most of the work with care and asked for help at the right moment. A little more checking at the end would make that good work even clearer.
Stories, practical tasks and discussions all showed steady effort. They are building a reliable way of working.
They joined in fully, and their ideas often moved a group forward. Keeping that energy for the quieter tasks will help them just as much.
The progress from the opening weeks to the close of term was easy to see. They should keep the routines that made it possible.
They are organised, kind in group work, and willing to try again when a first attempt is not the one they want. That is a strong base.
They understood the new ideas and could use them on a fresh example. Saying the steps out loud will help them catch the small slips.
good: They took part and finished the work they were set. Choosing one task each week to redo with more care would lift the parts that are still uneven.
There were good days of focus, especially when the task was practical. A short plan before written work would help those days become the usual pattern.
They show what they can do when they stay with a task. Beginning promptly has already made a difference.
Their contributions in discussion were thoughtful. Giving the same attention to finishing and checking will show that thinking on the page.
They have a sound grasp of the everyday work and they get on well with others. A few extra minutes on the current class work would help the ideas stick.
They tried, and several pieces of work were genuinely pleasing. The next gain is to keep that effort going on the days that feel harder.
needs_support: They are trying, and some pieces of work show real understanding. A quiet check-in at the start of each lesson will help them know where to begin.
They do better when the task is broken into small steps and someone looks at the first step with them. We will keep doing that in class.
Some ideas are already there, and they light up when the work is hands-on. We will use that strength while the written parts grow more slowly.
They need a little more time and a clear example before they work alone. With that, they can produce work they are pleased with.
Joining the short practice we send home will help. In class we will sit with them at the opening of each new topic.
They are not yet showing everything they can do. We will keep the work short, specific and encouraging so the next step feels possible.
urgent_support: They need more support than the usual lesson can give, and we will put that in place with the family. Please talk with us so we can agree what to practise together.
Small, daily practice on the current class work will help more than a long session now and then. We will send home one short activity at a time.
They are capable of more than this term has shown, and we will stay alongside them. A meeting to plan the support would be very welcome.
We will simplify the tasks, check in often, and celebrate each finished step. Please encourage them at home in the same way, without adding pressure.
The gap is in the foundations, not in their willingness. We will revisit those foundations in class, and we ask the family to keep the practice gentle and regular.
Please come in so we can look at the work together and choose the next step. They should know that the adults around them are on their side.

excellent: This was a term of real quality. They gave their best, and the people around them benefited from it.
The school is glad to see work of this care, and just as glad to see the kindness that came with it.
They set a tone others could follow: prepared, curious and fair. Please tell them we noticed.
A term like this comes from steady habits, not from one lucky week. Those habits are worth keeping.
They have shown what careful effort looks like. We hope they enjoy that feeling and carry it into the coming term.
It is a pleasure to sign a report that matches what their teachers have seen week after week. Well done.
very_good: A strong term, with effort that held up when the work got harder. We hope they keep that steadiness.
They have earned a quiet kind of pride. The school sees both the fruit of the effort and the way they treated other learners.
This is the sort of term that builds a reputation for reliability. Thank you for the support from home that makes it possible.
They are in a good place to stretch a little further. We will keep offering work that asks more of them, and we will keep the encouragement coming.
The term shows care, consistency and a willingness to join in. That combination matters as much as any single piece of work.
We are pleased. There is still room to polish the last details, and they are more than able to do that.
good: This was a worthwhile term. The school can see the effort, and we can also see where a little more finish would help.
They are moving in a good direction. We will keep the targets small and clear so the progress stays visible.
There is plenty to be pleased about, especially their willingness to take part. Regular practice of the current class work will help the rest catch up.
We thank them for the weeks that went well, and we will support the weeks that were harder. Please do the same at home.
A solid term, with room to grow. Choosing one area to improve, and staying with it, will be enough.
They belong in the conversation of the class, and their teachers enjoy teaching them. A steadier finish on written work is the next useful gain.
needs_support: They will benefit from a closer partnership between home and school. We are ready to plan that, and we will keep the plan realistic.
There is progress, and it needs protecting. Short, regular practice will do more than a burst of work at the end of a term.
We are not worried about their character. We do want more support around the learning, and we will say exactly what that support is.
Please sit with them for a few minutes of the current class work as often as you can. We will match that with extra attention in lessons.
This term asked a lot, and they need the adults to make the next steps smaller. We will do that here.
Encouragement, a clear routine and one target at a time will help. We will share that target so home and school are saying the same thing.
urgent_support: We want to meet soon. Together we can put a simple support plan around them, and we can review it while the term is still fresh.
Please know that this report is a request for partnership, not a judgement. They have adults who will stay with them.
The school will make the work smaller and check it more often. We ask the family to keep practice short, kind and regular.
They should hear, from all of us, that needing help is part of learning. We will make sure the help is actually there.
A fresh start in the daily routine, with support already arranged, is what we recommend. Please contact the school so we can set that up.
We will not wait for the next report to act. Extra help starts from this conversation, and we would like the family in it.
